purpose: Bank P simulator control (W97; GPT-6.1 review 7): re-run all four arms of frozen first tool-structure divergence states with a second user simulator, to check whether the W93 G/H/F picture of the core W4 cells is robust to the simulator.
scope: Robustness check on FIXED histories generated with the original simulator. Only the user simulator after the fork state changes. 80 states (40 if only batch 1 runs) and R = 5 per arm are too few to confirm or refute few-pp G/H/F effects; this is not a benchmark re-run and makes no claim about rates under the new simulator beyond these states.

eligibility.admission: analyze_ghf/analyze_dev admission, dev split only: snapshot gate, split guard (telecom holdout refused and never opened), quarantine, dedupe, strict complete-block rule (W70), complete 85-task retail/airline panel blocks (W78); divergent units only (Bank P = the first tool-structure divergence of the dev search; text-only differences are skipped by the search)
eligibility.recheck: re-checkable state: (1) the Q pivot replay at the state passed (state file q_replay: completion_ids_ok, prompt_ids_ok and action_ok all true); (2) the QQ no-op replay ran on this state (hash-selected noop sample of the dev fork, noop|state_id < noop_frac) and reproduced the original suffix, every suffix prompt-id sha, the termination reason and the step/error counters (analyze_dev.noop_ok checks suffix, prompts, termination, counters; its 'outcome' key is NOT consulted); (3) the BB, BQ and QB dev branches have prefix_ok and env_hash_init_ok. This is analyze_ghf's CASE_RULE eligibility without its outcome-based categories.

sampling_rule: Per cell (n = 20): two-level proportional allocation over the eligible states, both levels by largest remainder (Hamilton). Level 1: domains (retail, airline) in proportion to their eligible counts; ties in the remainder broken by sha256('simctrl-p-v1:alloc:' + model:cell + ':' + domain). Level 2: within a domain, its blocks in proportion to their eligible counts; ties broken by sha256('simctrl-p-v1:alloc:' + model:cell + ':' + domain + ':' + block). A stratum never receives more than it has. Within a stratum (domain, block) states are taken in ascending sha256('simctrl-p-v1:' + state_id). Batch 1 (10 per cell): per domain floor(k_d / 2) of its k_d selected states, the remaining slot(s) (0 or 1) to the domain with fewer selected states (ties: airline), so batch 1 is balanced by domain as far as possible; within a domain the states with the smallest sha256('simctrl-p-v1:' + state_id) go to batch 1. Batch 2 = the other 10. No outcome (Y, flips, G, H, I, rewards, terminations of any arm) is read by the selection.

user_llm.model: claude-sonnet-5-5 (headless claude -p, one clean call per user turn)

responder.daemon: scripts/a6000/simrelay_cli.py (login node; responder ids cli-<n>; default concurrency 12)
responder.call: claude -p --model claude-sonnet-5-5 --tools '' --strict-mcp-config --setting-sources '' --max-turns 1 --no-session-persistence --system-prompt <request system_prompt> --output-format json; cwd = an empty directory; user message on stdin; CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC=1; newest installed anthropic.claude-code-* binary
responder.isolation: one fresh headless call per user turn: no session, no tools, no MCP, no settings sources, empty cwd; no context shared across requests. Residual (identical for every request, no experiment identifiers): Claude Code appends its environment block (cwd, platform, date, model name) and an account-context reminder to the user message. Sampling settings are Claude Code's defaults (not controllable; adaptive thinking on); max_tokens is advisory.

template.header: You are the customer described in the system prompt. Below is the conversation so far. Write ONLY the customer's next message.
template.rule: header, then one block per message in order: role 'user' -> '<agent_label> <content>', role 'assistant' -> '<customer_label> <content>' (content stripped of surrounding whitespace), then a final '<customer_label>'; blocks joined by joiner; empty history -> empty_note in place of the blocks

responder.cleaning: strip only an accidental code fence, role prefix or surrounding quotes around the whole reply
responder.retries: up to 3 attempts per claim with backoff; then back to pending (cool-down); never a garbage answer

relay_protocol.req_id: 'v2-' + random uuid4 hex (no state, unit, arm or replicate identifiers)
relay_protocol.bookkeeping: sidecar <root>/meta/<req_id>.json (state_id, unit_id, arm, replicate, branch tag); never read by responders
relay_protocol.msg_sha256: sha256 of the canonical JSON (sort_keys, separators ',' ':', UTF-8) of the exact litellm message list incl. the system message
relay_protocol.on_mismatch: relay_call raises RelayIntegrityError: the branch fails as infra (missing, never imputed)

branches.XY: a_X (recorded in the frozen dev state file) forced at h_t, then controller Y (B = BF16, Q = the cell)
branches.replicates: R = 5 independent runs per arm per state; keyed '<arm>#<r>'; all 20 branches of a state run concurrently
branches.servers: B = BF16; Q = the cell's exact serving config (GPTQ/AWQ W4, calib c1), as the dev forks
branches.state_checks: state file sha; rebuilt state id, history sha, prompt-id sha equal the frozen file and the manifest; a_B/a_Q canonical shas; B regenerates a_B and Q regenerates a_Q exactly from the identical prompt ids (greedy); a failure makes the state missing
branches.Y: retail/airline: db_match and termination in (user_stop, agent_stop) (fork_driver._y)

unexposed: A branch that ends before any user-simulator call (n_user_calls == 0; e.g. the agent stops or the step budget ends after tool calls) is recorded exposed: false with its Y kept. It is NOT missing and does not fail the protocol check (relay checks apply only when n_user_calls > 0). Reported per arm; estimands are computed on all branches, and also on exposed-only as a sensitivity.

analysis_plan.per_state_arm_means: Ybar_s,XY = mean over the R = 5 replicates of arm XY on state s (complete replicates only).
analysis_plan.estimands: G = mean_s(Ybar_BQ - Ybar_QQ), H = mean_s(Ybar_QB - Ybar_QQ), F = mean_s(Ybar_BB - Ybar_QQ), G - H = mean_s(Ybar_BQ - Ybar_QB); per cell (equal weight per sampled state; the sample is proportionally stratified so no reweighting) and pooled over the 4 cells (equal weight per cell). Intervals: bootstrap over states within cell (B = 2000).
analysis_plan.simulator_change: Same states, original vs new simulator: original per-state arm outcomes from the frozen dev branch files (one run each; QQ = the recorded original continuation) vs the new arm means; report G/H/F/G-H under each simulator on the SAME 80 (or 40) states and their paired difference; per arm, the agreement of the original Y with the new replicate mean.
analysis_plan.within_simulator_variability: per arm, share of states whose 5 replicates are not all equal.
analysis_plan.not_allowed: The per-state four binary outcomes must NOT be summarised as an off-diagonal (Delta_Q != Delta_B) share comparable to W93's 26.9%: under a stochastic simulator with R = 5 replicate means the off-diagonal indicator is not the same quantity (noise alone creates off-diagonal patterns).
analysis_plan.reading: Robustness check only: whether the sign/size picture of G/H/F/G-H on these states survives the simulator change. It cannot confirm few-pp advantages (n = 80 states).
analysis_plan.missing: A state with a failed state check, or an arm-replicate with an infra error, is missing (never imputed); counts reported.

batches.rule: batch 1 = 10 per cell (40), batch 2 = the other 10 per cell (40); see sampling_rule.
batches.launch_rule: Batch 1 runs first. Batch 2 may be launched ONLY on throughput/time grounds (relay throughput, GPU and wall time available), decided without looking at any batch-1 outcome; if launched, the primary analysis uses all 80, otherwise the 40 of batch 1.

tasks.per_task: one task per cell per batch; q4: 1 GPU (gpu_util 0.44); q8: 2 GPUs pinned to node004/005/007; priority -14
